_about: Games added from 2026-10 (4 waves). tools/build_new_games.py turns this into the hub sections, menu, maps, i18n and SW cache. A game is published only when js/games/<id>.js exists. English first; other languages fall back to the English text.

sections.title: Cards & Board Games
sections.sub: The table games you know by heart, against a patient computer.

sections.title: Words & Numbers
sections.sub: Puzzles to sit down with, at your own pace.

sections.title: Nostalgia Trivia: the 50s to the 80s
sections.sub: Real songs, shows, faces and prices from the years we remember.

sections.title: Kitchen Table & Boardwalk
sections.sub: Pastimes from the kitchen table, the back of the placemat and the boardwalk. No clock unless you want one.

sections.title: Newspaper & Puzzle Book
sections.sub: The puzzles from the back pages, the placemat and the puzzle magazine. Pencil optional.

sections.title: Early Computers & Handhelds
sections.sub: Original takes on the first screen and handheld games. Every one waits for you.

sections.title: Retro Arcade
sections.sub: Original games in the spirit of the arcade classics. Slow to start, with big controls.

sections.title: Gentle Practice: linked to our articles
sections.sub: Calm, untimed games for enjoyment and practice. Each one has a short article about the research behind the idea - and what that research does not show.

games.title: FreeCell
games.desc: The solitaire where every card is face up.
games.inst: Tap a card, then tap where it goes. Each free cell holds one card.
games.why: Every card is visible, so it is all planning: thinking several moves ahead.

games.title: Spider Solitaire
games.desc: One suit: build runs from King down to Ace.
games.inst: Tap a card to move it with the cards on top of it. Tap Deal for a new row.
games.why: Keeping columns open for later is the whole game: planning with limited space.

games.title: Checkers
games.desc: The classic board game against a friendly computer.
games.inst: Tap your piece, then tap where it goes. If you can jump, you must.
games.why: Seeing what your opponent can do next is the skill behind every good move.

games.title: Backgammon
games.desc: Race your checkers home against the computer.
games.inst: Roll the dice, tap a checker, then tap a highlighted point.
games.why: Counting moves on the dice and weighing risks, roll after roll.

games.title: Dominoes
games.desc: The block game: match the ends and play out your hand first.
games.inst: Tap a domino that matches an open end. If it fits both ends, choose a side.
games.why: Matching numbers while keeping the tiles you will need later.

games.title: Crazy Eights
games.desc: Match the suit or the rank. Eights are wild.
games.inst: Tap a card that matches the top card. No match? Draw from the deck.
games.why: Watching suits and ranks change and saving your eights for the right moment.

games.title: Gin Rummy
games.desc: Make sets and runs, then knock before the computer does.
games.inst: Draw from the deck or the discard pile, then tap a card to throw away. Knock when your deadwood is 10 or less.
games.why: Grouping cards into sets and runs while remembering what has been thrown away.

games.title: Go Fish
games.desc: Ask for cards and collect sets of four.
games.inst: Tap a card in your hand to ask the computer for that rank.
games.why: Remembering what the other player asked for is how you win at Go Fish.

games.title: Hearts
games.desc: Dodge the hearts and the Queen of Spades against three computer players.
games.inst: Pass 3 cards, then follow suit when you can. Each heart is 1 point, the Q♠ is 13. Lowest score wins.
games.why: Counting which cards are gone and planning how to get rid of the dangerous ones.

games.title: Daily Mini Crossword
games.desc: A small American crossword with friendly clues.
games.inst: Tap a square, read the clue, and type with the big keyboard.
games.why: Matching a clue to a word that fits the letters you already have.

games.title: Cryptoquote
games.desc: Crack the letter code to reveal a famous American quote.
games.inst: Tap a code letter, then type the real letter. The same code letter is always the same real letter.
games.why: Spotting short words and common letters is how every newspaper puzzler cracks the code.

games.title: Word Ladder
games.desc: Change one letter at a time to climb from one word to another.
games.inst: Type a word that changes just one letter of the word above it. Reach the goal word.
games.why: Lewis Carroll's 1879 puzzle: searching your vocabulary one small step at a time.

games.title: Picture Logic
games.desc: Fill the grid by the numbers to reveal a picture.
games.inst: The numbers say how many squares in a row are filled. Tap a square to fill it.
games.why: Pure deduction: each number rules some squares in and others out.

games.title: Minesweeper
games.desc: Clear the field without touching a mine.
games.inst: Tap a square to open it. The numbers count nearby mines. Switch to Flag to mark one.
games.why: Reading the numbers around you to work out where it is safe.

games.desc: Slide and join matching tiles to reach 2048.
games.inst: Use the big arrows (or swipe) to slide all tiles. Equal tiles join.
games.why: Keeping your big tiles in a corner takes a plan, not luck.

games.title: Spot the Difference
games.desc: Real American street photos from the 1970s: find the five differences.
games.inst: Tap a difference on either picture. Take your time.
games.why: Comparing two scenes part by part is careful visual attention.

games.title: 15-Puzzle
games.desc: The sliding-tile puzzle from the toy box: put the numbers in order.
games.inst: Tap a tile in the same row or column as the gap to slide it. Arrow keys work too.
games.why: Getting one tile home without undoing the others takes a plan.

games.title: Mastermind
games.desc: The classic code-breaking game: find the hidden colors in 10 tries.
games.inst: Pick 4 pegs and tap Try. ● = right color, right place. ○ = right color, wrong place.
games.why: Each clue rules colors in or out: deduction, one try at a time.

games.title: Mancala
games.desc: The old stone-sowing board game, against a patient computer.
games.inst: Tap one of your pits. Its stones are sown one by one. Fill your store to win.
games.why: Counting where your last stone will land is the whole art of the game.

games.title: Dots and Boxes
games.desc: The pencil-and-paper game from the back of the placemat.
games.inst: Tap between two dots to pick a line, then tap Draw. Close a box to score and go again.
games.why: Avoiding the third side of a box, until the other player has to give one away.

games.title: Peg Jump Puzzle
games.desc: The wooden peg puzzle from the diner table: leave as few pegs as you can.
games.inst: Tap a peg, then tap an empty hole two steps away to jump over a peg and remove it.
games.why: Each jump changes which jumps are left, so a good finish is planned from the start.

games.title: Kitchen Table Dice
games.desc: Roll five dice up to three times and fill in the score card.
games.inst: Tap Roll, tap the dice you want to keep, roll again, then pick a line on the score card.
games.why: Weighing a sure score now against a bigger one later, roll after roll.

games.title: Boardwalk Roll
games.desc: The arcade-lane ball roll from the boardwalk: aim for the high rings.
games.inst: Put the aim mark where the ball should land, then tap Roll. Watch which way the lane leans.
games.why: Judging distance and direction, and adjusting after every ball.

games.title: Tower of Hanoi
games.desc: The toy-box disk puzzle: move the tower one disk at a time.
games.inst: Tap a peg to lift its top disk, then tap where it goes. Never put a big disk on a small one.
games.why: Small towers show the pattern that solves any size.

games.title: Eight Queens
games.desc: The chess-board puzzle: place queens so none can attack another.
games.inst: Tap a square to place a queen. No two may share a row, column or diagonal.
games.why: Every queen rules out whole lines of the board.

games.title: Knight's Tour
games.desc: Hop a chess knight onto every square of the board, once each.
games.inst: Tap a dotted square to jump in an L. Visit every square exactly once.
games.why: Corners and edges are hard to reach later, so visit them early.

games.title: Water Jugs
games.desc: Measure an exact amount with jugs that have no marks.
games.inst: Fill, empty or pour between jugs until one holds the amount asked for.
games.why: Pouring back and forth turns two sizes into any amount you need.

games.title: River Crossing
games.desc: The old riddles: get everyone across without trouble on either bank.
games.inst: Tap who goes in the boat, then Cross. Mind who is left alone together.
games.why: Sometimes the way forward is to bring someone back.

games.title: Balance Scale
games.desc: Find the one fake coin with only a few weighings.
games.inst: Put coins on the pans, press Weigh, and work out which coin is the fake.
games.why: Each weighing has three answers, so split the coins three ways.

games.title: Magic Square
games.desc: Fill the grid so every row, column and diagonal adds to the same total.
games.inst: Tap a square, then a number. Use each number once; every line must make the magic total.
games.why: Balancing many sums at once, one number at a time.

games.title: Number Pyramid
games.desc: Every brick is the sum of the two below it. Fill in the missing ones.
games.inst: Tap an empty brick and type its number. Two numbers in a little triangle give the third.
games.why: Adding up and taking away, one small triangle at a time.

games.title: Frog Swap
games.desc: Swap the frogs and toads on the lily pads, moving forward only.
games.inst: Tap a piece to hop onto the empty pad or jump over one of the other kind.
games.why: A tidy alternating pattern is the secret to never getting stuck.

games.title: Matchstick Fix
games.desc: The pub puzzle: move one match to make the sum true.
games.inst: Tap a lit match to pick it up, then tap an empty spot. Make the sum right with one move.
games.why: Seeing a digit as sticks opens up surprising answers.

games.title: Cage Math
games.desc: The puzzle-page number grid: every row and column once, every cage adds up.
games.inst: Fill each row and column with each number once. The numbers in every outlined cage must make its target with its sign.
games.why: Each cage narrows the choices; one sure number opens the next.

games.title: City Skyline
games.desc: Build the city so the edge numbers count the buildings you can see.
games.inst: Put a building of each height in every row and column. An edge number says how many buildings you can see from there.
games.why: Tall buildings hide short ones: a 1 always sits next to the tallest.

games.title: Island Bridges
games.desc: Join every island with straight bridges, as many as its number.
games.inst: Tap an island, then a neighbor in a straight line, to add a bridge. Give each island its number of bridges and join them all.
games.why: Start with the islands that have only one way to go.

games.title: Lamplighter
games.desc: Light every white square with lamps that never shine on each other.
games.inst: Tap a white square to put a lamp there. Light every white square; no two lamps may shine on each other.
games.why: Numbered walls tell you where lamps must go.

games.title: Campground
games.desc: Pitch one tent beside every tree, with the right count in each row.
games.inst: Tap a square next to a tree to pitch a tent. Tents never touch, and the edge numbers count the tents in each row and column.
games.why: Rows marked 0 turn straight into grass.

games.title: Drop Quote
games.desc: Put the fallen letters back in their columns to rebuild an old saying.
games.inst: Tap a square, then a letter from the pile under its column. Rebuild the saying row by row.
games.why: Short words like A, THE and IS are the easiest place to start.

games.title: Dot to Dot
games.desc: Join the numbered dots in order and watch a picture appear.
games.inst: Tap the dots in number order. A tap near the right dot counts.
games.why: Guess the picture before you finish it.

games.title: Fence Loop
games.desc: Draw one closed fence that fits every number in the field.
games.inst: Tap the gaps between dots to build fence. Make one closed loop; each number says how many of its square's sides are fence.
games.why: A 0 means no fence on any side: mark those first.

games.title: Garden Hose
games.desc: Turn the hose pieces until water reaches every flower.
games.inst: Tap a piece of hose to turn it. Join every piece to the faucet with no open ends.
games.why: Pieces at the edge of the garden can only face inward.

games.title: Parking Lot
games.desc: Slide the cars out of the way and drive the red car out of the gate.
games.inst: Tap a vehicle, then an arrowed square to slide it. Clear a path for the red car to the gate on the right.
games.why: Work backward: what is blocking the red car, and what is blocking that?

games.title: Golf Solitaire
games.desc: Clear the seven columns one card higher or lower at a time.
games.inst: Tap a bottom card that is one higher or one lower than the pile. Tap the stock when nothing fits.
games.why: Long runs up and down beat grabbing the first card that fits.

games.title: Pyramid Solitaire
games.desc: Take apart the pyramid in pairs that add up to 13.
games.inst: Tap two uncovered cards that add up to 13. A King goes away on its own.
games.why: Uncover the cards that free the most others first.

games.title: Accordion
games.desc: Fold a long row of cards into a few piles by suit and rank.
games.inst: Tap a pile, then the pile 1 or 3 places before it if the top cards match in suit or rank.
games.why: Sometimes waiting for a better jump folds more of the row.

games.title: Calculation
games.desc: Build four piles counting by ones, twos, threes and fours.
games.inst: Put each turned card on a foundation it fits, or on a waste pile. Suits never matter.
games.why: Keep one waste pile for Kings: they come last on every foundation.

games.title: Poker Squares
games.desc: Place 25 cards in a grid to score poker hands both ways.
games.inst: Tap an empty square to place each card. Every row and column scores as a poker hand.
games.why: Saving columns for one suit makes flushes while rows collect pairs.

games.title: High-Low Ladder
games.desc: Guess higher or lower to climb ten rungs with one deck.
games.inst: Tap Higher or Lower for the next card. Ten right guesses reach the top.
games.why: Remembering the cards already seen tells you what is left.

games.title: Kings in the Corner
games.desc: The family game: build down in alternating colors and empty your hand first.
games.inst: Draw, then tap a card and a pile it fits. Kings go in the corners. Tap End turn when done.
games.why: Moving a whole pile opens a space for any card.

games.title: Casino
games.desc: The old fishing card game: capture table cards that match or add up.
games.inst: Tap a card in your hand, then the table cards it captures, then Take. Or Trail to lay it down.
games.why: Watch for the Big and Little Casino: three points between them.

games.title: Spades
games.desc: Bid and take tricks with your partner; spades are always trump.
games.inst: Bid how many tricks you will take, then follow suit when you can. Spades beat everything.
games.why: Counting the spades played tells you when your King is safe.

games.title: Old Maid
games.desc: Make pairs and don't be left holding the last Queen.
games.inst: Tap a face-down card in the other player's hand to draw it. Pairs are thrown away.
games.why: Watching where the Old Maid goes is half the fun.

games.title: Finish the Song Title
games.desc: Complete the names of the hits of the 50s, 60s and 70s.
games.inst: Read the start of a famous song title and pick the missing words.
games.why: Bringing back the music you grew up with, one title at a time.

games.title: Who Sang It?
games.desc: Name the singer or group behind the hit.
games.inst: Read the song and the year, then pick who recorded it.
games.why: Linking a song to its singer is long-term memory at work.

games.title: Movie Quote Quiz
games.desc: Famous lines from the movies of the 60s to the 80s.
games.inst: Read the famous line and pick the movie it comes from.
games.why: A single line can bring back a whole film: recall from a small cue.

games.title: TV Trivia
games.desc: The American shows of the 60s, 70s and 80s.
games.inst: Read the question about a classic show and pick the right answer.
games.why: Remembering the shows, the characters and the places they were set.

games.title: Name That Year
games.desc: When did it happen? Pick the year.
games.inst: Read about a moment in history and pick the year it happened.
games.why: Placing events in time is how we organize what we remember.

games.title: Famous Faces
games.desc: Name the famous Americans of the era from their photos.
games.inst: Look at the photo and pick the person's name.
games.why: Putting a name to a face is one of the oldest memory skills we have.

games.title: Vintage Brands & Slogans
games.desc: The slogans and jingles we all heard on TV.
games.inst: Read the slogan and pick the brand that used it.
games.why: Slogans heard a thousand times stay with us: recall from a short cue.

games.title: Then vs Now Prices
games.desc: What did a stamp or a gallon of gas cost back then?
games.inst: Read the year and the item, then pick the price it really had.
games.why: Comparing then and now, with numbers from official records.

games.title: States & Capitals
games.desc: Name the capital of each of the 50 states.
games.inst: Read the state and pick its capital city.
games.why: The capitals we learned in school, brought back by practice.

games.title: Star Defender
games.desc: Hold back the rows of alien ships before they land.
games.inst: Move with the big arrows and press Fire. Shields protect you.
games.why: Timing your shots while watching the whole sky.

games.title: Space Rocks
games.desc: Turn, thrust and blast the drifting rocks.
games.inst: Turn left or right, press Thrust to move and Fire to shoot. Big rocks break into small ones.
games.why: Steering in every direction keeps your sense of space busy.

games.title: Paddle Tennis
games.desc: The first video game feeling: bat the ball past the computer.
games.inst: Drag the paddle or use the big buttons. First to 5 points wins.
games.why: Following a moving ball and meeting it in time.

games.title: Brick Breaker
games.desc: Bounce the ball and knock out the colored bricks.
games.inst: Move the paddle with your finger or the big buttons. Keep the ball in play.
games.why: Judging angles and getting there before the ball does.

games.title: Road Crossing
games.desc: Help the chicken cross the busy road and the river.
games.inst: Use the big arrows to hop. Wait for a gap in the traffic and ride the logs.
games.why: Waiting for the right moment is a skill in itself.

games.title: Shooting Gallery
games.desc: The fairground classic: tap the targets as they glide by.
games.inst: Tap the ducks and targets. Leave the bonus stars for extra points.
games.why: Spotting and tapping the right target quickly.

games.title: Snake
games.desc: Eat the apples and grow longer without hitting yourself.
games.inst: Turn with the big arrows or swipe. The snake starts slow.
games.why: Planning a path for a body that keeps getting longer.

games.title: Pop-Up Moles
games.desc: Tap the moles as they pop up from their holes.
games.inst: Tap a mole when it pops up. Leave the bunnies alone.
games.why: Reacting fast while holding back from the wrong target.

games.title: Name Garden
games.desc: Meet four neighbors, then see who is who. The answer is always shown.
games.inst: Tap a name for each neighbor. Ask to be shown at any time.
games.why: Matching a made-up name to something you can picture, with the right answer shown every time.

games.title: Pattern Workshop
games.desc: Copy a small mosaic at your own pace, with a rule example and Undo.
games.inst: Pick a piece, then pick a square. Turn pieces if the rule asks you to.
games.why: Looking carefully at shapes and how they turn, one small step at a time.

games.title: The Quiet Shelf
games.desc: Find the objects that match one clear rule on a calm shelf.
games.inst: Read the rule above the shelf, pick every match, then press Check shelf.
games.why: Searching a calm shelf for objects that match one rule.

games.title: A Day in Town
games.desc: Plan a few errands in a made-up town, or follow a small map.
games.inst: Choose Plan or Map. Pick stops in order, or follow the arrows on the map.
games.why: Putting a few errands in order, or following a route on a small map, with no clock.

games.title: Reversi
games.desc: The disc-flipping board game: trap the computer's discs to turn them your color.
games.inst: Tap a square with a ring. Every light disc trapped in a line flips to dark.
games.why: A corner, once taken, can never be flipped back: thinking a few moves ahead pays.

games.title: Four in a Row
games.desc: Drop checkers into the upright grid and line up four before the computer.
games.inst: Tap a column to choose it, then tap it again or press Drop. Four in a line wins.
games.why: Every checker is both an attack and a block: watching two plans at once.

games.title: Shut the Box
games.desc: The old pub dice game: shut the number tiles that add up to your roll.
games.inst: Roll the dice, tap tiles that add up to the roll, then press Shut them. Lowest total wins.
games.why: Choosing which tiles to shut now changes which rolls can still help later.

games.title: Light Switch Puzzle
games.desc: A grid of lamps where every press also flips the neighbors. Turn them all off.
games.inst: Tap a lamp: it and the lamps next to it switch. Make the whole board dark.
games.why: Order does not matter, only which lamps you press: a puzzle of pure logic.

games.title: Placemat Maze
games.desc: The pencil maze from the diner placemat: drive the car to the diner.
games.inst: Use the arrow buttons or tap a square in a straight line. Find the one true route.
games.why: Looking ahead for dead ends before you drive into them.

games.title: Nine Men's Morris
games.desc: The centuries-old mill game: line up three to take a piece.
games.inst: Place your 9 pieces, then slide them along the lines. Three in a row lets you remove a piece.
games.why: Building two mills at once, and spotting the computer's, is the heart of the game.

games.title: Sea Salvo
games.desc: The squared-paper fleet game: find and sink the hidden ships first.
games.inst: Tap a square on the enemy sea to aim, then tap again or press Fire. Sink every ship to win.
games.why: Each hit and miss narrows down where the rest of the fleet can be.

games.title: Bingo Night
games.desc: Community-hall bingo: daub your cards and call it before the other tables.
games.inst: Press Call the next ball, daub the number on your cards, and press BINGO! when a card has the pattern.
games.why: Keeping an eye on several cards at once, ball after ball.

games.title: Moon Landing
games.desc: The turn-by-turn lunar lander from the old computer terminals.
games.inst: Choose a throttle and fire for 5 seconds. Touch down gently before the fuel runs out.
games.why: Planning a steady descent with a limited fuel supply, one turn at a time.

games.title: Jelly Bean Jar
games.desc: The county fair guessing jar: how many beans are inside?
games.inst: Count or estimate the beans, type your guess, and win ribbons for close guesses.
games.why: Counting one row and multiplying is an old trick for a good estimate.

games.title: Six-Card Golf
games.desc: The kitchen-table card game where the lowest score wins, over three holes.
games.inst: Take the top discard or draw, then swap it into your six cards. Pairs in a column score zero.
games.why: Remembering what is under your face-down cards and building pairs in a column.

games.title: Cross Sums
games.desc: The number crossword from the puzzle magazines: every run adds up to its clue.
games.inst: Tap a white square and a digit. Each run adds up to its clue, with no digit twice.
games.why: Small sums can only be made one way: that is where every solve begins.

games.title: Logic Grid
games.desc: Who owns the canary? Work it out from the clues, puzzle-magazine style.
games.inst: Read the clues, pick a square in the table and tap the answer. Every puzzle has one solution.
games.why: Pure reasoning: each clue rules some answers in and others out.

games.title: Fill-In Puzzle
games.desc: No clues, just a word list: fit every word into the grid.
games.inst: Tap a square, then a word of the right length. Crossing words must share their letter.
games.why: Lengths and shared letters narrow every choice down.

games.title: Color by Number
games.desc: The paint-by-number pastime: fill each area with its numbered paint.
games.inst: Pick a paint, then tap the areas with its number. Finish to see the picture's title.
games.why: A calm, careful pastime: matching numbers to colors until the picture appears.

games.title: Chess
games.desc: Park-bench chess against a patient computer, with take-backs whenever you like.
games.inst: Tap a piece, then a dotted square. Checkmate the computer's king to win.
games.why: Every move is a small plan, and a take-back lets you try another one.

games.title: Rail Yard Shuffle
games.desc: The model railroader's switching puzzle: make up the train in the right order.
games.inst: Pick a siding, then choose how many cars the engine comes back out with. Build the train on siding A.
games.why: With short sidings, the order of moves is everything.

games.title: Twenty Questions
games.desc: Animal, vegetable or mineral? Find the hidden thing with yes-or-no questions.
games.inst: Ask questions from the list and cross things out. Guess it within the question limit.
games.why: A good question splits what is left in half.

games.title: Pick-Up Sticks
games.desc: The toy-box classic: lift each stick without disturbing the pile.
games.inst: Tap a stick, then Pick up. Only sticks with nothing on top of them come away cleanly.
games.why: Following one stick through the pile is careful, patient looking.

games.title: Tile Match
games.desc: Mahjong-style tile solitaire: clear the stack in matching pairs.
games.inst: Tap two free tiles with the same picture. A tile is free with nothing on top and one side open.
games.why: Choosing which pair to take first keeps the rest of the board open.
